title: Lingua Latina – frequency-based beginner course
source: Lemma choice and frequency ranks: DCC Latin Core Vocabulary (data/core_lemmas.json, CC BY-SA 3.0).
principles: Lessons are taught strictly in order; each one introduces 5–8 new lemmas and at most one new grammar rule.
Lemmas are chosen by DCC frequency rank AND teachability: function words and the commonest verbs/nouns first, but only when the grammar to use them has been taught.
A lesson may only use lemmas taught in this or earlier lessons, in forms unlocked by rules taught so far (scripts/validate_lesson enforces this).
30–50% of each lesson's exercises and drills recycle earlier lemmas for review (marked review: true).
A taught lemma is never re-introduced as new; proper names are allowed only from data/names.json and must be glossed in the lesson that first uses them.
Lessons 18 and 24 are consolidation lessons with no new grammar.

rules.title: Sentences with est – no articles
rules.summary: *est* means 'is'. Latin has no words for 'the' or 'a': *puella* = 'girl', 'the girl' or 'a girl'. A noun ending in -a (like *puella*) is the subject; an adjective describing her also ends in -a (*bona*). *nōn* goes before the word it negates.

rules.title: Plural subjects: -ae and sunt
rules.summary: More than one: *puella* → *puellae*, and *est* → *sunt* ('are'). Adjectives follow their noun: *puellae bonae*.

rules.title: Verbs: -t = he / she / it does
rules.summary: A verb ending in -t has a he/she/it subject: *stat* 'stands', *ridet* 'laughs'. The dictionary form ends in -ō (*stō*, *rīdeō*); -at verbs are 1st conjugation, -et verbs 2nd. The verb usually comes last.

rules.title: The object: -am
rules.summary: The person or thing on the receiving end (the direct object) changes its ending: *puella* → *puellam*. *Puella silvam videt* 'The girl sees the forest'. Because the ending marks the object, word order is free – but subject-object-verb is the usual pattern.

rules.title: Verbs: -nt = they do
rules.summary: A plural subject takes a verb in -nt: *puella labōrat* → *puellae labōrant*; *videt* → *vident*.

rules.title: Plural objects: -ās
rules.summary: One object -am, several objects -ās: *portam* → *portās*. Adjectives agree: *multās fābulās*.

rules.title: Second declension: -us, -ī, -um, -ōs
rules.summary: Masculine nouns like *servus* (and *puer*, *vir*): subject *servus* / plural *servī*; object *servum* / plural *servōs*. Adjectives describing them use the same endings: *servus bonus*, *servōs bonōs*.

rules.title: Neuter nouns: -um, plural -a
rules.summary: Neuter nouns (*bellum*, *dōnum*) look the same as subject and object: *-um* in the singular, *-a* in the plural. Adjectives agree: *dōnum novum*, *dōna nova*.

rules.title: Questions: -ne, quis?, quid?, cūr?
rules.summary: Add *-ne* to the first word to make a yes/no question: *Estne puella laeta?* Question words: *quis?* 'who?', *quid?* 'what?', *quem?* 'whom?', *cūr?* 'why?', *ubi?* 'where?'.

rules.title: I and you: -ō / -s; sum, es
rules.summary: The ending tells you the person: *amō* 'I love', *amās* 'you love', *amat* 'he/she loves'; *sum* 'I am', *es* 'you are'. *ego* and *tū* are only added for emphasis.

rules.title: We and you all: -mus / -tis; sumus, estis
rules.summary: *amāmus* 'we love', *amātis* 'you (all) love'; *sumus* 'we are', *estis* 'you are'. Now you know the whole present tense.

rules.title: Commands and calling someone
rules.summary: Command one person with the bare stem: *amā!*, *vidē!*; several people add -te: *amāte!*, *vidēte!*. When you call someone by name, -us becomes -e: *Mārce!*, *serve!*; other words don't change.

rules.title: The infinitive: to do (-āre, -ēre); possum
rules.summary: The infinitive is the 'to …' form: *amāre* 'to love', *vidēre* 'to see', *esse* 'to be'. It goes with verbs like *possum* 'I can' (*potest*, *possunt* …), *dēbeō* 'I must', *iubeō* 'I order'.

rules.title: Where to? ad, in, per, inter + accusative
rules.summary: Prepositions of motion take the accusative: *ad silvam* 'to the forest', *in silvam* 'into the forest', *per viās* 'through the streets', *inter puellās* 'among the girls'.

rules.title: The ablative: with, from, in
rules.summary: A new case for 'with / by / from / in': 1st declension *-ā / -īs*, 2nd *-ō / -īs*. *in silvā* 'in the forest', *cum amīcō* 'with a friend', *ex oppidō* 'out of the town', *sine aquā* 'without water'.

rules.title: The genitive: of (-ae, -ī)
rules.summary: 'Of': *puellae* 'of the girl', *puellārum* 'of the girls', *servī* 'of the slave', *servōrum* 'of the slaves'. It usually follows its noun: *via silvae* 'the path of the forest'.

rules.title: The dative: to / for (-ae, -ō, -īs)
rules.summary: The indirect object – to whom something is given or told: *puellae dōnum dat* 'he gives a gift to the girl'; *servō*, *servīs*. Verbs like *placeō*, *noceō*, *pāreō* take the dative.

rules.title: Third declension: rēx, rēgem, rēgēs
rules.summary: A big new noun family. The dictionary gives two forms: *rēx, rēgis* – the stem is in the second (*rēg-*). Object *rēgem*; plural subject and object *rēgēs*.

rules.title: Third declension: the other cases
rules.summary: *rēgis* 'of the king', *rēgī* 'to the king', *rēge* 'by/with the king'; plural *rēgum*, *rēgibus*. Some nouns (*urbs*, *mors*) have -ium in the genitive plural.

rules.title: Third declension neuters: corpus, nōmen
rules.summary: Neuters again have subject = object, plural in -a: *corpus* → *corpora*, *nōmen* → *nōmina*.

rules.title: Third conjugation: dīcō, dīcit, dīcunt
rules.summary: Verbs with infinitive -ere (short e): *dīcō, dīcis, dīcit, dīcimus, dīcitis, dīcunt*; command *dīc!* / *dūc!*, others *mitte!*; infinitive *dīcere*.

rules.title: faciō and audiō: -iunt
rules.summary: *faciō, facis, facit … faciunt* (3rd -iō) and *audiō, audīs, audit … audiunt* (4th). Infinitives *facere*, *audīre*.

rules.title: The imperfect: was doing, used to do (-bam)
rules.summary: Past ongoing action: *amābam* 'I was loving', *vidēbat* 'he was seeing', *dīcēbant* 'they used to say'; *eram* 'I was', *poteram* 'I could'.

rules.title: The future (1st & 2nd conj.): -bō, -bis, -bit
rules.summary: *amābō* 'I will love', *vidēbit* 'he will see'; *erō, eris, erit* 'I will be'; *poterō* 'I will be able'.

rules.title: The future (3rd & 4th conj.): -am, -ēs, -et
rules.summary: *dīcam* 'I will say', *dīcēs*, *dīcet* …; *audiam*, *audiet*; *faciam*, *faciet*. Careful: *dīcet* (will say) vs *dīcit* (says).

rules.title: The perfect: did, have done
rules.summary: The third dictionary form gives the perfect stem: *amāvī* 'I loved', *vīdit* 'he saw', *dīxērunt* 'they said', *fuit* 'was'. Endings -ī, -istī, -it, -imus, -istis, -ērunt.

rules.title: Me, to me, with me: ego, tū, nōs, vōs
rules.summary: *mē* 'me', *mihi* 'to me', *tē*, *tibi*, *nōs*, *nōbīs*, *vōs*, *vōbīs*; *mēcum* 'with me'.

rules.title: is, ea, id: he, she, it, that
rules.summary: *is* 'he', *ea* 'she', *id* 'it'; *eum*, *eam* 'him, her'; *eius* 'his/her'; *eī* 'to him'; plural *eī, eae, ea*, *eōs, eās*.
